root_cause.text: The pNFS `pnfs_roc()` path unconditionally performed a blocking wait on `NFS_LAYOUT_RETURN_LOCK` during delegation return in `open()`, because non-blocking/sync state from the caller was not propagated, creating a circular dependency with NFSv4 state recovery.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that delegreturn waited for a layout return “that cannot complete because a state recovery was initiated” and that recovery “cannot complete until the open() finishes,” and the patch fixes this by adding a `bool sync` parameter to `pnfs_roc()`, passing `wait/issync` from callers, and changing `pnfs_roc()` so `if (test_bit(NFS_LAYOUT_RETURN_LOCK, ...))` it avoids `wait_on_bit()` when `!sync`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that delegreturn waited for a layout return “that cannot complete because a state recovery was initiated” and that recovery “cannot complete until the open() finishes,” and the patch fixes this by adding a `bool sync` parameter to `pnfs_roc()`, passing `wait/issync` from callers, and changing `pnfs_roc()` so `if (test_bit(NFS_LAYOUT_RETURN_LOCK, ...))` it avoids `wait_on_bit()` when `!sync`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the wait flag to pnfs_roc() during NFSv4 close so return-on-close processing honors the requested wait behavior.
intent_record.what: The call to pnfs_roc() in nfs4_do_close() was changed from passing four arguments to passing five, adding the local wait parameter as the new final argument while reformatting the call across lines.
intent_record.how: This allows pnfs_roc() to receive the caller's wait mode during close processing, so the layout return-on-close setup can follow the requested blocking or non-blocking behavior instead of using only the previous argument set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the delegreturn synchronous-state flag to pnfs_roc() so pNFS ROC handling behaves correctly for sync and async delegreturn paths.
intent_record.what: The call to pnfs_roc(inode, &data->lr.arg, &data->lr.res, cred) was changed to pass an additional argument, issync, becoming pnfs_roc(inode, &data->lr.arg, &data->lr.res, cred, issync).
intent_record.how: This change propagates the issync flag into pnfs_roc() during delegreturn processing, allowing that function to distinguish synchronous from non-synchronous cases and handle return-on-close state accordingly instead of always operating without that context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend pnfs_roc to accept a new boolean sync argument for caller-controlled runtime behavior.
intent_record.what: The function declaration and definition of pnfs_roc were changed from taking four parameters to taking five by adding a new final parameter, `bool sync`, while reformatting the signature across two lines.
intent_record.how: This change extends the pnfs_roc interface so callers can pass an explicit boolean synchronization/control flag at runtime, enabling the function implementation or downstream logic to distinguish between sync modes if used, without showing any other behavior change in this hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the default `false` initialization of `skip_read` so its later computed value is used correctly in `pnfs_roc()`.
intent_record.what: The local boolean variable `skip_read` in `pnfs_roc()` was changed from being explicitly initialized to `false` at declaration to being declared without an initializer.
intent_record.how: This removes the forced default value so `skip_read` must be assigned later before use, which can preserve the actual result of subsequent control flow or helper logic instead of preemptively setting it to false.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix pnfs_roc() to avoid stale layout-header handling on the no-ROC delegation path and ensure skip_read is initialized consistently.
intent_record.what: The change removes a call to pnfs_get_layout_hdr(lo) and deletes the subsequent check for NFS_LAYOUT_RETURN_LOCK that unlocked inode/RCU locks, waited on the NFS_LAYOUT_RETURN bit, released the layout header reference with pnfs_put_layout_hdr(lo), and retried. It also adds an explicit initialization of skip_read to false before delegation checks, and in the case where both read and write delegations are present, sets lo = NULL before jumping to out_noroc.
intent_record.how: At runtime, pnfs_roc() no longer waits and retries when a layout-return lock flag is set on the layout header, so that synchronization path is removed from this location. The explicit skip_read initialization prevents use of a stale or uninitialized value before the delegation logic updates it. Setting lo to NULL before the out_noroc path when both delegations are held ensures the function exits that path without carrying a layout header pointer, avoiding incorrect downstream handling of lo.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix pnfs_roc() to avoid invalid or redundant layout returns and to safely coordinate with concurrent layout return operations.
intent_record.what: The change adds several new checks in pnfs_roc(): when an open state has FMODE_WRITE, it now sets lo to NULL before jumping to out_noroc; when any open state has FMODE_READ, it records skip_read and then newly scans lo->plh_segs to see whether any layout segment is not IOMODE_READ, aborting return-by-close by setting lo to NULL and jumping out if all segments are read-only; it also now takes a layout header reference with pnfs_get_layout_hdr(lo) and checks NFS_LAYOUT_RETURN_LOCK in lo->plh_flags, either recording deferred return info with pnfs_set_plh_return_info(lo, skip_read ? IOMODE_RW : IOMODE_ANY, 0) for async cases or dropping locks, waiting on NFS_LAYOUT_RETURN, releasing the layout header, and retrying for sync cases before continuing to iterate layout segments.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents return-on-close from proceeding when writable open state exists, avoids attempting a layout return when the caller only has read opens and the layout contains only read segments, and serializes against an in-progress layout return so concurrent return operations do not race. In async mode it defers/merges the return request, and in sync mode it waits for the current return to finish and retries safely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the caller-provided sync mode for pnfs_layoutcommit_inode() in pnfs_roc() instead of always forcing a synchronous layout commit.
intent_record.what: The call to pnfs_layoutcommit_inode() in pnfs_roc() was changed to pass the variable sync instead of the constant true.
intent_record.how: This makes the layout commit operation follow the function's sync setting at runtime rather than always forcing synchronous behavior, allowing the caller's intended commit mode to be honored.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend pnfs_roc with a sync flag so callers can control synchronous versus non-synchronous operation.
intent_record.what: The declaration of pnfs_roc in the header was changed from taking four parameters (struct inode *ino, struct nfs4_layoutreturn_args *args, struct nfs4_layoutreturn_res *res, const struct cred *cred) to taking a fifth parameter, bool sync, while also reformatting the prototype across two lines.
intent_record.how: This changes the function interface so callers can explicitly specify a synchronous mode flag when invoking pnfs_roc, enabling different runtime behavior based on whether the operation should run synchronously or not; code using the old signature must be updated to compile and pass the new control value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend pnfs_roc to accept a sync flag while leaving the current stub behavior unchanged.
intent_record.what: The definition of the static inline function pnfs_roc was reformatted from a multi-line declaration to a single-line function name line with aligned parameters, and its signature was extended by adding a new final parameter `bool sync`; the function body remains unchanged and still returns `false`.
intent_record.how: This changes the function interface so callers can pass a synchronization flag, enabling future or external logic to distinguish sync behavior at call sites or in alternate implementations, but in this stub implementation runtime behavior remains unchanged because the function still always returns `false` and does not use the new parameter.
